subject: Re: Short pilot top-up and SLA credit request
messages:
From: Geo Patel <geo@stellardata.com>
To: David Kim <david_kim@redwood.ai>
Cc: procurement@stellardata.com
Date: Mon, 21 Jun 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Short pilot top-up and SLA credit request

Hi David,

Thanks again for the demo last week — the team at Stellar Data has been putting the Redwood runtime through a short stress pass as we finalize our internal evaluation. A couple of things came up we want to align on before we expand the test: 

- We’re going to need an extra 2 weeks on the pilot to finish integration and run heavy inference tests (roughly equivalent to an additional 40 GPU-hours).
- Given the bursty nature of our workload, we’d like to request a one-time top-up with a modest discount and a performance credit if tail latency exceeds the thresholds we measured this week.

I attached a short usage report (usage_report_q2.pdf) showing the pattern. High-level ask is: can you extend the pilot window by 14 days (time-boxed) and provide a 20% discount on the top-up hours, plus a service credit structure if the 95th percentile latency is above 300ms for >5% of requests during the extension? Procurement is looped.

Happy to sync live if that helps.

Best,
Geo
Head of ML Eng, Stellar Data

-- attachment: usage_report_q2.pdf (PDF, 420KB)
From: David Kim <david_kim@redwood.ai>
To: Geo Patel <geo@stellardata.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 22 Jun 2026 14:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Short pilot top-up and SLA credit request

Hi Geo — thanks for the clear note and the attachment. Appreciate the usage slice, that helps.

We can accommodate a 14-day time-boxed top-up. To make sure we protect both parties and keep it simple for procurement, here are two options we can offer today: 

Option A — Top-up (recommended):
- 40 GPU-hours add-on, applied to your existing pilot window (14 days).
- 20% one-time discount off the list top-up rate.
- Performance credit: if 95th percentile latency > 300ms for >5% of requests during the extension, we will apply a 10% credit to the top-up invoice.
- No changes to full MSA; we’ll attach a one-page addendum for signatures.

Option B — Short-term Dedicated Trial (if you expect sustained bursting):
- 30-day burst window with capacity reservation and a higher hourly commitment. Pricing differs; requires procurement approval.

For speed, I drafted a one-page addendum that codifies Option A (attached: addendum_stellardata_v1.docx). If you and procurement are comfortable, we can send the DocuSign link and get this live today.

Quick question for the team: is the 300ms threshold the right lever here, or would Stellar prefer a throughput-based guard (e.g., >X tokens/sec sustained for Y minutes)? Either is fine — just want to align to avoid ambiguity in measurement.

If it helps, we can also add a short rollback clause: if the extension uncovers quality regressions we’ll pause the test and support a focused remediation run.

Thanks — I’ll wait on your confirmation.

Cheers,
David Kim
Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference

-- attachment: addendum_stellardata_v1.docx (DOCX, 18KB)
From: David Kim <david_kim@redwood.ai>

Date: Tue, 22 Jun 2026 16:30:00 -0700
Subject: Fwd: Short pilot top-up and SLA credit request — approval check

Marissa / Karthik — forwarding Geo’s ask and my proposed Option A (20% discount on 40 hours + 10% performance credit if 95th >300ms for >5% of requests). Quick context: Stellar is a mid-market prospect with clear ramp potential; this is a low-dollar, short-duration concession to keep momentum.

Revenue impact: ~40 hours at list -> ~$6k gross; with 20% discount net ~$4.8k (approx). We expect expansion if they confirm post-eval.

Risk: performance credit caps total concession impact; addendum is time-boxed and limited to this pilot top-up only.

Approve to proceed with Option A and send DocuSign? If yes, I’ll include a simple acceptance email for procurement and push for signature today.

Thanks,
David

Geo — thanks for the quick turn. Procurement confirmed and we’re good to proceed on Option A with the measurement threshold you suggested (95th percentile > 300ms for >5% of requests).

Summary of agreed terms (time-boxed addendum):
- Extension: +14 days to the current evaluation window (time-boxed).
- Top-up: 40 GPU-hours applied to the pilot; 20% one-time discount.
- Performance credit: if 95th >300ms for >5% of requests during extension, Redwood will apply a 10% invoice credit to the top-up.
- Measurement: Redwood will provide the latency report daily and final consolidated report at the end of the extension.
- Effective once the addendum is signed (DocuSign link below).

DocuSign: https://www.docusign.com/Signing/StartSigning?docId=abc123
HubSpot deal: https://app.hubspot.com/deal/DEAL-7892

I’ve attached the final addendum and will send DocuSign for signature now. Once signed we’ll provision the hours and start the monitoring dashboard for you.

Appreciate the partnership — looking forward to the next steps.

Best,
David Kim
Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference
